discoveries.scope: Design the Rust harness discovery workflow: five useful interactive tools, durable human feedback, and evidence-bound completion.

blindspots.title: A prose field cannot represent a decision
blindspots.observation: Before currently stores unknowns and alternatives as strings. The original artifact renderer cannot distinguish options, answers or semantic pairs.
blindspots.consequence: Five prettier pages would still be summaries. There would be nothing meaningful to select or carry into implementation.
blindspots.constraint: Use typed findings, intervention alternatives, questions, semantic mappings and plan choices.

blindspots.title: Clicks do not update the repository
blindspots.observation: The HTML runs as a local standalone file; no server or filesystem write authority is attached.
blindspots.consequence: A human could believe an answer was recorded while the agent continues from old requirements.
blindspots.constraint: Label browser changes as draft proposals. Export JSON and require explicit task-artifact decide import.

blindspots.title: An open tab can describe an old decision set
blindspots.observation: A reviewer can keep several artifact tabs open while an agent publishes new content or imports another page.
blindspots.consequence: Old choices could silently overwrite newer decisions or refer to options whose meaning changed.
blindspots.constraint: Bind exports to the task, discovery hash and feedback history hash. Reject stale inputs and reopen regenerated pages.

blindspots.title: The artifact cannot certify its own final verification
blindspots.observation: All checked-in JSON and HTML participate in the workspace fingerprint used by CI.
blindspots.consequence: Inserting a final report hash into source after CI invalidates that report.
blindspots.constraint: Finalize source artifacts before CI. Keep final source-bound reports under target; never treat a quiz or copied prompt as approval.

interventions.title: Keep the existing prose pages
interventions.approach: Retain the five string fields and improve typography only.
interventions.benefit: Very small implementation and migration cost.
interventions.tradeoff: Does not satisfy the requested discovery interactions; retain as a comparison, not the selected solution.

interventions.title: Typed offline discovery tools
interventions.approach: Add strict section models, five fixed interactive renderers and explicit feedback import.
interventions.benefit: Real comparisons and answers become durable decisions with no service dependency.
interventions.tradeoff: Requires schema migration, rich fixtures and interaction tests.

interventions.title: Task-authored custom HTML
interventions.approach: Allow agents to generate bespoke scripts and visualizations for every task.
interventions.benefit: Maximum task-specific expressiveness, including arbitrary simulations.
interventions.tradeoff: Harder to validate interactions and safe rendering; authored JavaScript executes in the reviewer context.

interventions.title: Connected review service
interventions.approach: Host task artifacts with authenticated live writes to task state.
interventions.tradeoff: Adds deployment, authentication and network prerequisites beyond this local Rust starter.

questions.prompt: Which discovery tools are required for every task?
questions.why: This determines the schema and admission checks, so it must be settled before implementation.

options.label: The five selected discovery tools
options.consequence: Blindspots, interventions, interview, reference map and tweakable plan are required.

options.label: One generic unknowns summary
options.consequence: Smaller surface but fails the requested interaction depth.

settled.basis: The user explicitly named these five as mandatory, then requested implementation.

questions.prompt: How should browser reactions become durable decisions?
questions.why: Local HTML cannot silently edit repository files. This choice determines the write boundary.

options.label: Explicit export and CLI import
options.consequence: Offline, inspectable and compatible with source-bound evidence.

options.label: Live writes through a local server
options.consequence: Convenient but adds server lifecycle and access-control requirements.

settled.basis: The accepted implementation proposal described revision-checked feedback import; no server is required.

questions.prompt: Which optional discovery tool would be most useful next?
questions.why: This is exploratory follow-up, not a blocker for the five requested tools.

options.label: An interactive domain explainer
options.consequence: Useful when terminology or behavior is unfamiliar.

options.label: A live interaction mock
options.consequence: Useful when UX cannot be decided from prose.

options.label: Competing visual design directions
options.consequence: Useful when layout or style is undecided.

reference.name: Existing task-artifact lifecycle and source examples
reference.revision: Local inspected implementation at f78c3c15 plus current uncommitted HTML lifecycle work
reference.target: discovery.rs, discovery_feedback.rs and five discovery renderers

mappings.behavior: Preserve the original snapshot and append revisions
mappings.source_excerpt: Artifact { before: Before, notes: Vec<Note>, publications: Vec<Publication> }
mappings.target_excerpt: Artifact { before, notes, publications, discoveries: Vec<Discovery>, feedback: Vec<Feedback> }
mappings.difference: Keep existing preflight bytes semantically unchanged. Add discovery and response histories instead of replacing old assumptions.
mappings.expected: After two discovery revisions, the original before and first discovery remain intact; rewriting committed history fails handoff.

mappings.behavior: Invalidate a publication after its inputs change
mappings.target_excerpt:
notes_count matches
AND discovery_sha256 matches
AND feedback_sha256 matches
mappings.difference: A final brief must reflect both implementation notes and the current discovery/decision state.
mappings.expected: Importing valid feedback makes completion fail until the brief and quiz are republished.

mappings.behavior: Self-contained HTML backed by validated data
mappings.source_excerpt: read JSON → validate → deterministic HTML → exact-byte check
mappings.target_excerpt: typed discovery → five independent HTML tools → exported proposal → validated import
mappings.difference: Browser interactions are new; arbitrary task-authored code remains unsupported. Exports are data, not execution instructions.
mappings.expected: Script-like authored text is displayed as text. Wrong-task, stale or unknown-choice exports do not mutate record.json.

choices.title: How should discovery content be represented?
choices.why: Interaction requires distinct concepts that the current Before strings cannot encode.

options.label: Typed sections
options.tradeoff: Strong validation and meaningful controls; more types to maintain.
options.preview:
struct Discovery {
  blindspots: Vec<Blindspot>,
  interventions: Vec<Intervention>,
  interview: Interview,
  reference: Reference,
  plan: Plan,
}

options.label: Five free-text sections
options.tradeoff: Minimal schema, but cannot reliably model options or semantic relationships.
options.preview:
struct Discovery {
  blindspots: String,
  interventions: String,
  interview: String,
  reference: String,
  plan: String,
}

choices.title: Where do human choices enter the source record?
choices.why: This is the boundary between exploration and changing task intent.

options.label: Revision-checked import
options.tradeoff: Explicit and offline; the human must export and supply the JSON.
options.preview:
Browser draft
  → Export JSON(task, discovery hash, feedback base)
  → task-artifact decide
  → append Feedback
  → regenerate artifacts

options.label: Live service
options.tradeoff: Immediate collaboration but requires authentication and service operation.
options.preview:
Browser
  → authenticated API
  → concurrent state store
  → synchronized task records

choices.title: How should historical tasks be handled?
choices.why: A new mandatory workflow must not manufacture preflight work for old tasks.

options.label: Versioned active admission
options.tradeoff: Keep old records readable; migrate resumed tasks explicitly.
options.preview:
v1–v3 archived → readable history
v4 active → all five tools required
resumed legacy → labeled current discovery

options.label: Rewrite all historical records
options.tradeoff: Uniform schema but misrepresents earlier work and expands migration scope.
options.preview:
Every archived task
  → generated replacement preflight
  → rewritten history (not recommended)

steps: Define strict discovery and feedback types with source references.
Render five distinct tools with selection summaries and downloadable responses.
Import feedback only for matching task and current revision; append it.
Gate active v4 records and invalidate final publication when inputs change.
Exercise CLI and actual UI code, then run full CI and completion.
mechanical: Regenerate affected HTML after renderer changes.
Refresh the exact policy transition receipt before final CI.

before.outcome: Review unknown-discovery prompts and select an HTML task lifecycle.
before.unknowns: Retrospective migration: the original review happened before this artifact feature existed. Which source prompts should be mandatory was the original uncertainty.
before.assumptions: This snapshot is not evidence of pre-review timing.
before.alternatives: The initial optional HTML recommendation was rejected; the user chose mandatory HTML with four lifecycle views.
before.verification: See the retained assessment and the implementation task regression evidence.

notes.observation: The user rejected optional HTML after the initial prompt review.
notes.decision: Implement mandatory HTML for all active tasks, with preserved preflight, accumulating notes, buy-in and quiz.
notes.effect: The historical assessment is retained with a superseding policy link; implementation and validation are in html-tasks. This is a retrospective record, not a backdated preflight.

notes.observation: The user required richer interactive discovery rather than the previous summary page. This task record is being explicitly resumed under v4; its original preflight and earlier notes remain intact.
notes.decision: Add the five structured discovery tools and use the current source examples as a concrete migration. Preserve previous publications and append an updated brief.
notes.effect: Unknowns now opens a discovery index. Human choices can be exported and imported as revision-bound append-only feedback; prior preflight timing is not fabricated.

content.change: Three subagents reviewed the eight pre-implementation prompts, the implementation-notes prompt, and both post-implementation prompts. The user selected mandatory HTML rather than the original optional presentation recommendation.
content.demonstration: The selected implementation is demonstrated by harness/task-artifacts/html-tasks/index.html. This review record is a retrospective migration and does not claim its preflight preceded the original assessment.
content.verification: The review is retained in docs/unknowns-review.md; implemented behavior is verified by the task-artifacts acceptance tests. Final CI is separate.
content.risks: The illustrative source artifacts do not establish measured comprehension benefits. Human usefulness still needs observation during adoption.

quiz.question: What does a correct quiz answer establish?
options: The task is approved for merge.
Understanding of that question; approval and verification remain separate.
quiz.explanation: The quiz never modifies task records, CI evidence or approval state.

content.change: Generic unknowns prose is replaced by five mandatory interactive tools: blindspots, interventions, interview, reference semantics and tweakable plan. Task v4 and artifact v2 preserve existing histories while representing findings, questions and choices directly.
content.demonstration: The generated-UI test selects constraints and interventions, enters and revisits a custom interview answer, highlights matched semantics, exports a correction, changes a plan preview and imports each actual export through the real CLI. Replaying an old export fails, and reopening the plan shows recorded decisions.
content.verification: Rust CLI regressions pass for required artifacts, malformed/stale feedback, wrong-task imports, publication invalidation, unanswered blocking questions and history preservation. The actual generated scripts pass DOM integration. Final source-bound CI/completion reports are separate under target/verification/discovery-workbench. Native layout and clipboard/download behavior still require human browser review.
content.risks: Feedback actors are declared, not authenticated. Browser drafts do not modify the repository until explicit import. Opening an old tab after another import requires refreshing; imports deliberately reject stale feedback rather than guessing how to merge it. The five requested discovery tools are implemented; optional domain explainers, mock builders and visual design explorations remain future work.

quiz.question: Does selecting an option in the HTML change the repository?
options: No. Export decisions and explicitly import the JSON.
Yes. Every click immediately writes the task record.
quiz.explanation: The page holds draft proposals. task-artifact decide validates and appends an explicit import.

quiz.question: A second artifact was open before feedback from the first was imported. What happens to its old export?
options: It silently replaces the newer decisions.
It is rejected; reopen the regenerated page and export again.
quiz.explanation: The feedback-history hash prevents old tabs from overwriting a newer decision context.

quiz.question: Does the recommended plan preview count as a human selection?
options: No; an explicit selection is required for export.
Yes; the default preview is automatically approved.
quiz.explanation: Recommendations and sourced existing answers are labeled. The renderer does not invent new human approvals.
